title: API Error Response Design That Works

scenes.line1: What makes a great API error?
scenes.say: What makes a great API error response? How should you structure it so clients can actually use it?

scenes.label: Clarity
scenes.sub: Structured errors help clients debug fast.
scenes.say: Clear, structured error responses help clients debug and handle problems gracefully.

rows.b: A URI for the error type

scenes.say: Use the RFC 7807 standard. Include a type URI, a short title, the HTTP status code, and a detailed explanation.

scenes.title: Problem Details JSON
scenes.say: Here’s how a real error response looks. Each field gives clients actionable info.

scenes.question: What’s missing in this error response?
scenes.wrong: Just a status code is enough.
scenes.right: Clients need type, title, status, and detail.
scenes.say: Interview trap: Is a status code enough? Nope. Clients need a type, title, status, and detail to handle errors well.
